purpose: Orchestrate a validated scene into eight purposeful cinematic perceptions, adapting frame purpose and POV to narrative state while preserving the canonical eight-frame production contract.
core_principle: Eight frames are a controlled cinematic sequence, not a fixed shot template. The director adapts perception, information release, emotional progression, and visual emphasis to the scene's causal structure.

adaptive_director_model.deviation_policy: The director may replace or reorder default frame purposes only when a causal narrative reason exists and the deviation is recorded.
adaptive_director_model.deviation_limit: No more than three frame-purpose deviations without explicit scene-level override.
nonnegotiables: F01 establishes sufficient canonical reality for audience orientation unless a justified cold-open deviation is recorded.
At least one frame must expose the dominant character's perception.
At least one frame must expose a meaningful counter-perception when multiple active characters have conflicting interpretations.
Turning point must be represented by a distinct frame.
F08 must establish a stable ending state or a deliberate narrative hook.
No frame may introduce information unavailable to its assigned perspective.
All frame transitions must have a causal or perceptual reason.

frame_director_schema.perspective: AUDIENCE or canonical character ID or SHARED
frame_director_schema.transition_reason: why this frame follows the previous frame
frame_director_schema.adaptation_reason: why this frame differs from default template, if applicable

director_rules: Use CSD-009 only after a PASS or approved PASS_WITH_ADVISORIES.
Never invent a frame to fill the eight-slot contract.
Frame purpose must derive from scene causality or perception progression.
POV assignment must derive from CSD-008 and CSD-007.
Emotional progression must derive from CSD-006.
Character participation must derive from CSD-005.
Do not duplicate adjacent frames unless repetition is deliberately used for escalation, emphasis or contrast.
A frame may be visually quiet when the narrative state requires internal processing.
A frame may use shared perspective when no single character has exclusive perceptual priority.
Camera variation must support perception; camera variation alone is not adaptation.
If a scene is action-dominant, temporal compression may replace exposition while preserving causal clarity.
If a scene is introspection-dominant, visual micro-performance may replace overt action.
If information is withheld, the frame should encode absence or ambiguity rather than fabricate certainty.

demo_test.title: The Meaning of Restraint
demo_test.adaptive_reason: The scene is introspection-dominant after an external power escalation is deliberately suppressed; therefore the director reduces overt action and increases micro-performance, perception contrast and information withholding.

frame_plan.attention_target: three-character relationship geometry and contained energy
frame_plan.information_revealed: Ravana has restrained his power; no physical escalation is occurring
frame_plan.transition_reason: establish shared canonical reality before entering subjective perception
frame_plan.audience_effect: know tension has changed but not why it matters yet

frame_plan.transition_reason: move from objective reality into the dominant character's interpretation
frame_plan.audience_effect: suspect the contest has become psychological
frame_plan.adaptation_reason: replaces generic introduction with subjective reading because character state is already established

frame_plan.information_revealed: Hanuman confirms no immediate intervention is required
frame_plan.transition_reason: counter-perception verifies the threat from a protector's information state
frame_plan.audience_effect: feel safety without losing latent danger
frame_plan.adaptation_reason: uses witness POV instead of a second generic character introduction

frame_plan.reaction: no external reward or fear appears
frame_plan.transition_reason: turns external power into internal question
frame_plan.audience_effect: feel uncertainty inside the dominant character
frame_plan.adaptation_reason: replaces action escalation with micro-performance because CSD-006 identifies introspective state

frame_plan.information_revealed: all three read the same physical event differently
frame_plan.transition_reason: synchronize the competing perceptions without changing reality
frame_plan.adaptation_reason: shared perspective is necessary to compare interpretations without privileging one

frame_plan.attention_target: Rama's calm as evidence against Ravana's old belief
frame_plan.information_revealed: visible dominance has not produced the expected reaction
frame_plan.transition_reason: objective evidence now presses against the established misbelief
frame_plan.adaptation_reason: compresses conventional escalation into psychological escalation

frame_plan.information_revealed: Rama recognizes the state change without humiliating him
frame_plan.reaction: Ravana is left with his own choice
frame_plan.transition_reason: the protagonist's controlled non-action becomes the causal turning point
frame_plan.audience_effect: feel the power shift from force to mastery
frame_plan.adaptation_reason: turning point is expressed through deliberate non-action rather than combat

frame_plan.information_revealed: the encounter has changed Ravana's internal state
frame_plan.information_withheld: what he will ultimately do with that insight
frame_plan.transition_reason: end on changed state rather than external spectacle
frame_plan.audience_effect: feel closure of the encounter and curiosity about Ravana's next choice
frame_plan.camera_intent: controlled closing portrait with environmental scale
frame_plan.adaptation_reason: uses a hook because CSD-006 identifies unresolved emotional continuity
